The Physics, in One Paragraph

Ceramic stores heat and radiates it softly — great for a custard pie that shouldn't weep, great for even top browning, mediocre for setting a fruit pie's bottom before juice soaks it. Metal does the opposite: it slams heat into the crust the second it hits, which is what lattice-top fruit pies need. Neither is "better." They solve different pies.

What the Reviews Actually Show

Both listings are strong by any bar we set (4.7+ with thousands of ratings — these cleared our curation gates the same way every product on the site does). The recurring praise splits exactly along the physics: the ceramic reviews are full of serving-photos and "baked evenly"; the metal reviews are full of "finally a brown bottom." The recurring complaints split too: ceramic owners occasionally report thermal-stress chips from hot-to-cold shock; metal owners note single-pan purchases during two-pie holidays.

Which One Should You Buy?

USA Pan — fruit pies are your benchmark dish, and a pale bottom crust keeps ruining an otherwise good pie.

LE TAUCI two-pack — you're baking pumpkin and apple for a full table, and you want one dish that goes from oven to table without a stopover.
